Then my enemy will see and will be covered with shame— she who said to me, “Where is the LORD your God?” My eyes will see her; at that time she will be trampled like mud in the streets.
So to this day Israel has been in rebellion against the house of David.

verses.text: How long, O LORD? Will You hide Yourself forever? Will Your wrath keep burning like fire?

xrefs.text: How long, O LORD? Will You be angry forever? Will Your jealousy burn like fire?
Fire consumed His young men, and their maidens were left without wedding songs.
I will wait for the LORD, who is hiding His face from the house of Jacob. I will put my trust in Him.
Truly You are a God who hides Himself, O God of Israel, the Savior.
Why, O LORD, do You reject me? Why do You hide Your face from me?

verses.text: Remember the briefness of my lifespan! For what futility You have created all men!

xrefs.text: [“]Man, who is born of woman, is short of days and full of trouble.
Please remember that You molded me like clay. Would You now return me to dust?
Remember that my life is but a breath. My eyes will never again see happiness.
My days are swifter than a runner; they flee without seeing good.
Man is like a breath; his days are like a passing shadow.

verses.text: What man can live and never see death? Can he deliver his soul from the power of Sheol? Selah

xrefs.text: By faith Enoch was taken up so that he did not see death: “He could not be found, because God had taken him away.” For before he was taken, he was commended as one who pleased God.
But God will redeem my life from Sheol, for He will surely take me to Himself. Selah
For the living know that they will die, but the dead know nothing. They have no further reward, because the memory of them is forgotten.
before the dust returns to the ground from which it came and the spirit returns to God who gave it.
No man can possibly redeem his brother or pay his ransom to God.

verses.text: Where, O Lord, is Your loving devotion of old, which You faithfully swore to David?

xrefs.text: But My loving devotion will never be removed from him as I removed it from Saul, whom I removed from before you.
but Jesus became a priest with an oath by the One who said to Him: “The Lord has sworn and will not change His mind: ‘You are a priest forever.’”
Incline your ear and come to Me; listen, so that your soul may live. I will make with you an everlasting covenant— My loving devotion promised to David.

I will make known the LORD’s loving devotion and His praiseworthy acts, because of all that the LORD has done for us— the many good things for the house of Israel according to His great compassion and loving devotion.
The LORD swore an oath to David, a promise He will not revoke: “One of your descendants I will place on your throne.

verses.text: Remember, O Lord, the reproach of Your servants, which I bear in my heart from so many people—

xrefs.text: Remember how the enemy has mocked You, O LORD, how a foolish people has spurned Your name.
Rise up, O God; defend Your cause! Remember how the fool mocks You all day long.
because zeal for Your house has consumed me, and the insults of those who insult You have fallen on me.
For even Christ did not please Himself, but as it is written: “The insults of those who insult You have fallen on Me.”
You have made us a reproach to our neighbors, a mockery and derision to those around us.

verses.text: how Your enemies have taunted, O LORD, and have mocked every step of Your anointed one!

xrefs.text: If you are insulted for the name of Christ, you are blessed, because the Spirit of glory and of God rests on you.
How long, O God, will the enemy taunt You? Will the foe revile Your name forever?
How is it to your credit if you are beaten for doing wrong and you endure it? But if you suffer for doing good and you endure it, this is commendable before God.
Still others endured mocking and flogging, and even chains and imprisonment.
We work hard with our own hands. When we are vilified, we bless; when we are persecuted, we endure it;

verses.text: Blessed be the LORD forever! Amen and amen.

xrefs.text: Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, from everlasting to everlasting. Amen and Amen.
Blessed be the LORD God, the God of Israel, who alone does marvelous deeds.
Now to the King eternal, immortal, and invisible, the only God, be honor and glory forever and ever. Amen.
Though the fig tree does not bud and no fruit is on the vines, though the olive crop fails and the fields produce no food, though the sheep are cut off from the fold and no cattle are in the stalls,
Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, from everlasting to everlasting. Let all the people say, “Amen!” Hallelujah!
